In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
eL12 and eL12 are eukaryotic L7 proteins which are present in the cytoplasm of Artemia salina.
the eL12 protein is an L7/L12-like protein, which occurs as a dodecamer and is associated with 60-S ribosomes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
eL12 and eL12 are present in a large excess over the 60-S subunits and that the eL12 protein is present in the cytosolic pool.
eL12 is a dimeric protein with a molecular weight of 35,000 and is present in a large quantity in the cytoplasm.
in the eukaryotic cell there are two different L7/L12 proteins, eL12 and eL12’, which differ in their amino acid sequences, but which are very closely related in structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the eL12 proteins of A. salina and rat are structurally and functionally similar to L7/L12 proteins of prokaryotic ribosomes.
the eL12 proteins from rat liver and A, salina have similar physical and biochemical characteristics and are similar in size to the eL12 of the Escherichia coli 50-S subunit.
the eL12 protein of A. salina and rat is a member of the L12 family of eucaryotes.
